While I was all set to write a two star review for this, the "Eek! Methinks not" descriptor seemed a bit better. While I guess that the teenagers who work at this time warp to the 1980s were fairly friendly, I think I'm going to steer clear of this place again. It wears its years very poorly and nothing appears to have been updated since the 1990s. 

I'll admit that I don't particularly enjoy 3D film for the sake of 3D film, nor do I enjoy paying an extra 3 bucks for it. Because the Grandin Theatres don't have 3D capabilities, all of the films are shown in 2D at all times. The prices are low, on all fronts as well.

We walked into the theatre when all of the lights were on and it was a scary sight - who knows how much gum there is stuck on the floors and under the seats? Additionally, we couldn't see the entire film, either because of an obstruction on the projector or an issue with the placement of the screen.

I'm very happy paying the extra cash to see a new blockbuster at the Cineplex Odeon North or the Scotiabank Theatre at the West Edmonton Mall.

Love this place. That is really it. It is a little rundown and sort of hidden in corner, but it is clean. I don't remember how we discovered this little gem, but I am glad we did. I can live without the 3D option a lot of movies seem to be filmed in, you're still watching the same storyline. The concession is reasonably priced. Our last visit consisted of a kid's combo and a two drinks, one popcorn combo for $14. That alone makes this place worth it. 

They still have matinee prices, weekday and weekend, and Tuesday is $5.00. They show the newer movies, so you aren't going there for movies that have been out for months and months. 

Just know that they don't take debit or credit. It is cash only. They have an ATM in the lobby because I can never get to a bank before hand.
It's a nice little mom & pop theatre.  Prices are slightly lower than most and with a coupon from the SUTP book it's awesome!  Always had great customer service here as well :-)

Grandin Theatres is horrible.  I can forgive a lot for an inexpensive theatre ticket, but not when it comes to this place.  The floors are a sticky mess, the lights in cinema two are on the fritz and dim and illuminate throughout the screening of films for no reason in particular, soundproofing between the cinemas is poor, the patrons have full volume conversations during screenings, the projectors are horribly outdated and produce blurry images on the screen, and the screens themselves seem to be too small to accommodate the aspect ratios of the films, so images bleed over from the screen onto the adjacent walls.  Forget this place.  Pay full freight at a proper cinema.  Life is too short to save money on this kind of subpar theatre environment.

This movie theatre is located in St. Albert. I discovered it by chance, and now come here quite often. Grandin Theatre is never too busy, except at opening nights for new blockbusters. I have noticed that most employees are very young boys and girls but the quality of service doesn't suffer because of that. The seats at Grandin are rather comfortable, and all auditoriums are kept relatively clean. The screens are large, and the sound is good. Couple times there were incidents when the movie didn't start on time or when the volume wasn't set loud enough, but it wasn't something a friendly talk with one of the employees couldn't fix. The major thing that makes Grandin irresistible is the fact that tickets for all the latest movies are cheaper than at all other movie theaters. They are $7.50 but don't quote me on that. This theater is worth checking out, definitely!
Closed as of May 31. Sad to see one of the last independently owned theatres bite the dust. This time next year it'll be a construction zone for a new building.
